Method: Cat 1 — Purchased goods & services — Average-data EF
Equation (canonical):
Emissions = Σ (mass of purchased good/service × EF per unit mass)
OR
Emissions = Σ (units of purchased good/service × EF per reference unit)
Activity data required (fields): • Mass or number of units of purchased goods or services for a given year (e.g., kg, hours spent, pieces)
EF/parameters required (factor keys): • Cradle-to-gate emission factors of the purchased goods or services per unit of mass or unit of product (e.g., kg CO2e/kg or kg CO2e/hour spent)
Calculation steps:
1) For each purchased good/service type, capture activity data as either mass (kg) or units (piece/hour/etc.).
2) Select a cradle-to-gate EF in matching units.
3) Multiply activity × EF.
4) Sum across purchased goods and services.

Method: Cat 1 — Purchased goods & services — Hybrid (only supplier S1+S2 + waste + residual EF)
Equation (canonical):
Emissions = Σ supplier_scope1+2_allocated
+
Σ (supplier_waste_mass × EF_waste_activity)
+
Σ (purchased_good_mass_or_units × EF_purchased_good_excl_supplierS1S2_and_waste)
Activity data required (fields):
• Allocated scope 1 and scope 2 emissions of tier 1 supplier relating to purchased good/service (kg CO2e)
• Mass of waste from tier 1 supplier relating to purchased good (kg)
• Mass or quantity of units of purchased good/service (kg, units, or $ basis depending on EF)
• Reporting year; mapping from supplier to purchased items
EF/parameters required (factor keys):
• EF_waste_activity (kg CO2e/kg waste)
• EF_purchased_good_excluding_supplier_scope1_scope2_and_supplier_waste (kg CO2e/kg OR per unit OR per $)
Calculation steps:
1) Collect supplier-allocated Scope 1+2 emissions for the purchased good/service.
2) Collect supplier waste outputs attributable to the purchased good/service (kg).
3) Select EF for waste activity (kg CO2e/kg) consistent with end-of-life boundary.
4) Compute waste emissions = waste_mass × EF_waste.
5) Collect purchased good quantity (kg/units) (or $ if EF is value-based).
6) Select residual EF for the purchased good that explicitly EXCLUDES supplier scope 1, scope 2, and supplier waste emissions.
7) Compute residual emissions = quantity × residual EF.
8) Total = supplier S1+S2 + waste emissions + residual emissions. Sum across goods/services.

Method: Cat 1 — Purchased goods & services — Hybrid (supplier activity data for all activities)
Equation (canonical):
Σ supplier scope 1&2 (allocated to purchased good/service)
+
Σ (material inputs × EF_material)
+
Σ (incoming transport distance × mass/volume × EF_vehicle)
+
Σ (supplier waste outputs × EF_waste)
+
other emissions as applicable
Activity data required (fields):
• Allocated scope 1 and 2 data (including emissions from electricity use and fuel use and any process and fugitive emissions) by supplier relating to the good or service purchased
• Mass or quantity of material inputs (bill of materials) used by supplier to produce purchased goods
• Mass or quantity of fuel inputs used by supplier to produce purchased goods (if needed to support supplier scope 1 allocation)
• Distance from origin of raw material inputs to supplier (exclude supplier→reporting company transport; that is Category 4)
• Quantities of waste output by supplier to produce purchased goods
• Other emissions emitted in provision of the purchased goods as applicable
EF/parameters required (factor keys):
Depending on supplier data availability, may need:
• Cradle-to-gate emission factors for materials used by tier 1 supplier (supplier-specific or industry-average secondary database)
• Life cycle emission factors for fuel used by incoming transport of input materials to tier 1 supplier
• Emission factors for waste outputs by tier 1 supplier
• Other emission factors as applicable (e.g., process emissions)
Also, if product-level factors are used instead of component build-up, collect either:
• Cradle-to-gate EF per unit mass/unit product (kg CO2e/kg, kg CO2e/unit)
OR
• Cradle-to-gate EF per unit economic value (kg CO2e/$)
Calculation steps:
1) Collect allocated Scope 1 and 2 emissions of tier 1 supplier relating to the purchased good/service.
2) Collect bill of materials (mass/quantity of material inputs used by tier 1 supplier for the purchased good/service).
3) For each material input, multiply input quantity × cradle-to-gate EF for the material.
4) Collect incoming transport data for material inputs to tier 1 supplier (distance, mass/volume, vehicle type).
5) For each transport leg, compute: distance × mass/volume × vehicle EF.
6) Collect waste outputs by tier 1 supplier relating to the purchased good/service and multiply by waste EFs.
7) Add any other applicable emissions in provision of the good/service.
8) Sum all components across purchased goods and services.

Equation (canonical): Emissions = Σ (value of purchased good/service ($) × EF per unit economic value (kg CO2e/$))
Activity data required (fields): • Amount spent on purchased goods or services, by product type, using market values (e.g., $)
EF/parameters required (factor keys): • Cradle-to-gate emission factors of the purchased goods or services per unit of economic value (e.g., kg CO2e/$)
Calculation steps:
1) Extract spend by product type (market value) for reporting year.
2) Map spend categories to an EF category.
3) Select cradle-to-gate EF (kg CO2e/$).
4) Multiply spend × EF and sum.

Method: Cat 1 — Purchased goods & services — Supplier-specific EF
Equation (canonical): Σ (quantities of good purchased × supplier-specific product emission factor of purchased good or service)
Activity data required (fields): • Quantities or units of goods or services purchased
EF/parameters required (factor keys): • Supplier-specific emission factors for the purchased goods or services (e.g., from a reliable cradle-to-gate GHG inventory, product footprint, or internal LCA report)
Calculation steps:
1) For each purchased good/service, get quantity purchased (e.g., kg or units).
2) Get supplier-specific product emission factor for the purchased good/service (e.g., kg CO2e/kg).
3) Multiply quantity × supplier EF.
4) Sum across purchased goods and services.

Equation (canonical):
Emissions = Σ (mass of capital good × EF per unit mass)
OR
Emissions = Σ (units of capital good × EF per reference unit)
Activity data required (fields): • Mass or number of units of capital goods for a given year (e.g., kg, pieces)
EF/parameters required (factor keys): • Cradle-to-gate emission factors of the capital goods per unit of mass or unit of product (e.g., kg CO2e/kg or kg CO2e/piece)
Calculation steps:
1) Capture capital goods purchased by type as mass or units.
2) Select matching cradle-to-gate EF.
3) Multiply activity × EF.
4) Sum across capital goods.

Equation (canonical): Emissions = ∑(quantity_capital_goods × EF_avg_capital_good)
Activity data required (fields): reporting_year; capital_good_type; quantity; unit
EF/parameters required (factor keys): avg_cradle_to_gate_ef (kgCO2e/kg or per unit)
Calculation steps:
1) Identify capital goods purchased in reporting year per capitalization policy.
2) Capture quantity (kg/units) by capital good type.
3) Select average cradle-to-gate EF.
4) Multiply quantity × EF.
5) Sum across capital goods.

Method: Cat 2 — Capital goods — Hybrid (only supplier S1+S2 + waste + residual EF)
Equation (canonical):
Emissions = Σ supplier_scope1+2_allocated
+
Σ (supplier_waste_mass × EF_waste_activity)
+
Σ (capital_good_mass_or_units × EF_capital_good_excl_supplierS1S2_and_waste)
Activity data required (fields):
• Allocated scope 1 and scope 2 emissions of tier 1 supplier relating to capital good (kg CO2e)
• Mass of waste from tier 1 supplier relating to the capital good (kg)
• Mass or quantity of units of capital good (kg, units, or $ basis depending on EF)
• Reporting year; mapping from supplier to capital goods
EF/parameters required (factor keys):
• EF_waste_activity (kg CO2e/kg waste)
• EF_capital_good_excluding_supplier_scope1_scope2_and_supplier_waste (kg CO2e/kg OR per unit OR per $)
Calculation steps:
1) Collect supplier-allocated Scope 1+2 emissions for the capital good.
2) Collect supplier waste outputs attributable to the capital good (kg).
3) Select EF for waste activity (kg CO2e/kg).
4) Compute waste emissions = waste_mass × EF_waste.
5) Collect capital good quantity (kg/units) (or $ if value-based EF).
6) Select residual EF for capital good that explicitly excludes supplier S1+S2 and supplier waste emissions.
7) Compute residual emissions = quantity × residual EF.
8) Total = supplier S1+S2 + waste emissions + residual emissions. Sum across capital goods.

Method: Cat 2 — Capital goods — Hybrid (supplier activity data for all activities)
Equation (canonical):
Σ supplier scope 1&2 (allocated to capital good)
+
Σ (material inputs × EF_material)
+
Σ (incoming transport distance × mass/volume × EF_vehicle)
+
Σ (supplier waste outputs × EF_waste)
+
other emissions as applicable
Activity data required (fields):
• Allocated scope 1 and 2 data by supplier relating to the capital good purchased (incl. electricity, fuel, process, fugitive)
• Mass/quantity of material inputs used by supplier to produce capital goods
• Mass/quantity of fuel inputs used by supplier to produce capital goods
• Distance from origin of raw material inputs to supplier (exclude supplier→reporting company transport; that is Category 4)
• Quantities of waste output by supplier to produce capital goods
• Other emissions emitted in provision of capital goods as applicable
EF/parameters required (factor keys):
Depending on supplier data availability:
• Cradle-to-gate EFs for materials used by tier 1 supplier (supplier-specific or industry-average)
• Life cycle EFs for fuel used by incoming transport of input materials to tier 1 supplier
• EFs for waste outputs by tier 1 supplier
• Other EFs as applicable (process emissions)
Also, if using product-level factors instead of component build-up:
• Cradle-to-gate EF per unit mass/unit product OR per $
Calculation steps:
1) Collect allocated supplier Scope 1+2 emissions for the capital good.
2) Collect material inputs and compute Σ(material_qty × EF_material).
3) Collect incoming transport of material inputs and compute Σ(distance × mass/volume × EF_vehicle).
4) Collect supplier waste outputs and compute Σ(waste_mass × EF_waste).
5) Add other applicable emissions.
6) Sum all components across capital goods.

Equation (canonical): Emissions = Σ (value of capital good ($) × EF per unit economic value (kg CO2e/$))
Activity data required (fields): • Amount spent on capital goods, by product type, using market values (e.g., $)
EF/parameters required (factor keys):
• Cradle-to-gate emission factors of the capital goods per unit of economic value (e.g., kg CO2e/$)
• Inflation data where applicable to convert market values between EEIO EF year and activity year
Calculation steps:
1) Extract spend on capital goods by type.
2) Map spend type to EF category/EEIO sector.
3) Normalize spend to EF base year if required.
4) Multiply spend × EF and sum.

Equation (canonical): Emissions = Σ (quantities of capital good purchased × supplier-specific product emission factor of capital good)
Activity data required (fields): • Quantities or units of capital goods purchased in the reporting year
EF/parameters required (factor keys): • Supplier-specific emission factors for the capital goods (e.g., from reliable cradle-to-gate GHG inventory, product footprint, internal LCA report)
Calculation steps:
1) For each capital good type, capture quantity purchased (kg or units).
2) Obtain supplier-specific product EF for the capital good (kg CO2e/kg or per unit), cradle-to-gate.
3) Multiply quantity × EF.
4) Sum across capital goods.

Method: Cat 3A — Upstream emissions of purchased fuels
Equation (canonical):
Σ (fuel consumed × upstream fuel emission factor)
where upstream fuel emission factor = life cycle emission factor − combustion emission factor
Activity data required (fields): • Quantities and types of fuel consumed
EF/parameters required (factor keys):
Supplier-specific method:
• Fuel-provider-specific emission factors on extraction, production and transportation of fuels per unit of fuel consumed (e.g., kg CO2e/kWh), by fuel type and country/region
Average-data method:
• Average emission factors for upstream emissions per unit of consumption (e.g., kg CO2e/kWh)
Calculation steps:
1) For each fuel type consumed, capture quantity consumed.
2) Select upstream fuel emission factor (supplier-specific if available; otherwise average-data).
3) If only lifecycle + combustion are available, compute upstream EF = lifecycle − combustion.
4) Multiply fuel consumed × upstream EF.
5) Sum across fuel types.

Method: Cat 3B — Upstream emissions of purchased electricity/steam/heating/cooling
Equation (canonical):
Emissions = Σ(electricity_consumed × EF_upstream_electricity)
+ Σ(steam_consumed × EF_upstream_steam)
+ Σ(heating_consumed × EF_upstream_heating)
+ Σ(cooling_consumed × EF_upstream_cooling)
where upstream EF = life cycle EF − combustion EF − T&D losses (subtract T&D only if included in life cycle EF)
Activity data required (fields): • Total quantities of electricity, steam, heating or cooling purchased and consumed per unit of consumption (e.g., kWh/MWh), broken down by supplier, grid region or country
EF/parameters required (factor keys):
Supplier-specific method:
• Utility-specific EFs for extraction, production and transportation of fuels consumed per unit generated (kg CO2e/kWh)
Average-data method:
• Grid-region/country/regional upstream EFs per unit consumption (kg CO2e/kWh)
Plus (if deriving upstream EF):
• life cycle EF
• combustion emissions factor
• T&D losses inclusion flag
Calculation steps:
1) Collect electricity/steam/heating/cooling consumption, broken down by supplier/region/country.
2) Select upstream emission factors per energy type (supplier-specific if available; else grid-region/country/regional).
3) If provided as lifecycle EFs, verify whether T&D losses are included.
4) If upstream EF must be derived, compute upstream EF = lifecycle − combustion − (T&D losses if included).
5) Multiply consumption × upstream EF for each energy type and sum.

Equation (canonical):
Emissions = Σ(electricity_consumed × EF_lifecycle_electricity × T&D_loss_rate)
+ Σ(steam_consumed × EF_lifecycle_steam × T&D_loss_rate)
+ Σ(heating_consumed × EF_lifecycle_heating × T&D_loss_rate)
+ Σ(cooling_consumed × EF_lifecycle_cooling × T&D_loss_rate)
Activity data required (fields): • Electricity, steam, heating or cooling consumed (kWh/MWh), broken down by grid region or country; and/or • Scope 2 emissions data
EF/parameters required (factor keys):
• Life cycle emission factor for each energy type (kg CO2e/kWh)
• T&D loss rate (%)
Supplier-specific: utility-specific T&D loss rate for the grid
Average-data: country/regional/global T&D loss rate
Calculation steps:
1) Collect consumption by energy type and grid region/country.
2) Select lifecycle EF for each energy type.
3) Select appropriate T&D loss rate (utility-specific preferred; else country → regional → global).
4) Multiply consumption × lifecycle EF × loss rate and sum across energy types.

Equation (canonical): Emissions = Σ(volume_stored × avg_days_stored × EF_storage (kg CO2e per m³-day or pallet-day or TEU-day))
Activity data required (fields):
• Volume of purchased goods stored (m²/m³/pallet/TEU) OR number of pallets
• Average number of days stored
• Throughput-based data (as needed to estimate volume-days)
EF/parameters required (factor keys):
• Storage emission factor per unit stored per day, expressed as:
  - kg CO2e per pallet-day, OR
  - kg CO2e per m²-day / m³-day, OR
  - kg CO2e per TEU-day
Calculation steps:
1) Estimate storage volume and average storage duration (days).
2) Select appropriate storage EF matching the unit basis.
3) Multiply volume × days × EF.
4) Sum across storage facilities.

Equation (canonical):
Facility emissions = (fuel_kWh × EF_fuel) + (electricity_kWh × EF_electricity) + (refrigerant_leakage_kg × GWP)
Allocated facility emissions = (volume_company_goods_m3 / total_volume_goods_m3) × facility_emissions
Total emissions = Σ allocated facility emissions
Activity data required (fields):
• Site-specific fuel use (kWh)
• Site-specific electricity use (kWh)
• Site-specific refrigerant leakage (kg)
• Average occupancy rate / average total volume stored
• Volume of reporting company’s purchased goods in facility (m³)
• Total volume of goods in facility (m³)
EF/parameters required (factor keys):
• Site/region-specific EFs for fuels (kg CO2e/kWh) and electricity (kg CO2e/kWh)
• Refrigerant GWP / emission factors (kg CO2e/kg leaked)
Calculation steps:
1) Compute storage facility emissions from fuel, electricity, and refrigerant leakage.
2) Allocate emissions by volume share of reporting company goods.
3) Sum allocated emissions across all storage facilities.

Equation (canonical): Emissions = Σ(mass_or_volume_goods × distance_leg_km × EF_mode_or_vehicle (kg CO2e per tonne-km or TEU-km))
Activity data required (fields):
• Mass or volume of products transported (tonnes or TEU)
• Distances travelled per leg (supplier provided, maps/calculators, port-to-port distances)
• Mode of transport / vehicle type per leg
EF/parameters required (factor keys): • Emission factor by transport mode or vehicle type, in units of CO2/CH4/N2O per tonne-km or TEU-km (convert to CO2e as needed)
Calculation steps:
1) Collect transport legs with mass/volume, distance, and mode/vehicle.
2) Select EF per mode/vehicle.
3) Multiply mass/volume × distance × EF per leg.
4) Sum across modes/vehicle types.

Equation (canonical):
Emissions = Σ(fuel_litres × EF_fuel)
+ Σ(electricity_kWh × EF_electricity_grid)
+ Σ(refrigerant_leakage_kg × GWP_refrigerant)

If fuel data unavailable:
Fuel_from_spend = fuel_spend / avg_fuel_price
Fuel_from_distance = Σ(distance_km × fuel_efficiency_l_per_km)

Allocated fuel use = total_fuel_consumed × (mass_or_volume_company_goods / mass_or_volume_total_goods)
(Optional) Unladen backhaul emissions = Σ(fuel_backhaul × EF_fuel)
Activity data required (fields):
• Quantities of fuel consumed (litres) by fuel type; OR fuel spend + avg fuel price; OR distance travelled + fuel efficiency
• Quantity of electricity consumed (kWh) (if applicable)
• Quantity of refrigerant leakage (kg) (if applicable)
• Mass of purchased goods in the vehicle (tonnes) and total mass/volume transported (for allocation)
• Info on refrigerated transport (yes/no)
• (Optional) distance travelled unladen + unladen fuel efficiency
EF/parameters required (factor keys):
• Fuel emission factors (kg CO2e/litre) (include scope 1 & 2 of fuel; may optionally include cradle-to-gate)
• Electricity grid emission factors (kg CO2e/kWh) for electric vehicles
• Refrigerant leakage factors: GWP per refrigerant (kg CO2e/kg leaked)
• Average fuel price ($/litre) (if deriving fuel from spend)
• Fuel efficiency (litre/km) (if deriving fuel from distance)
Calculation steps:
1) Collect direct fuel litres by type; if missing derive from spend or distance.
2) Compute total transport emissions: fuel + electricity + refrigerant leakage.
3) Allocate emissions to reporting company: multiply by mass/volume share (or dimensional/chargeable mass if justified).
4) Optionally add unladen backhaul emissions if included.
5) Sum across fuel types and transport steps.

Equation (canonical): Emissions = Σ(spend_on_transportation_by_type × EEIO_EF_transport (kg CO2e/$))
Activity data required (fields):
• Amount spent on transportation by type (road/rail/air/barge/etc.) using market values ($)
• (If needed) inflation data to convert between EEIO EF year and activity year
EF/parameters required (factor keys):
• Cradle-to-gate emission factors of transportation type per $ (kg CO2e/$)
• Inflation indices (if required)
Calculation steps:
1) Collect spend by transportation type.
2) Map spend types to EEIO categories.
3) Normalize spend to EEIO base year if required.
4) Multiply spend × EF and sum.

Method: Cat 5 — Waste generated in operations — Average-data (treatment mix)
Equation (canonical): Σ (total mass of waste (tonnes) × proportion of total waste treated by waste treatment method × emission factor of waste treatment method (kg CO2e/tonne))
Activity data required (fields):
• Total mass of waste generated in operations
• Proportion of this waste being treated by different methods (e.g., % landfilled, incinerated, recycled, etc.)
EF/parameters required (factor keys): • Average waste treatment-specific emission factors based upon all waste disposal types (kg CO2e/tonne)
Calculation steps:
1) Record total mass of waste generated (tonnes).
2) Record treatment shares for each method (% landfill/incineration/recycling/etc.).
3) Select EF per treatment method (kg CO2e/tonne).
4) Multiply total mass × share × EF for each method.
5) Sum across treatment methods.

Method: Cat 5 — Waste generated in operations — Supplier-specific (waste treatment company)
Equation (canonical): Σ allocated scope 1 and 2 emissions of waste treatment company
Activity data required (fields): • Allocated scope 1 and 2 emissions of waste-treatment company (allocated to the waste collected from the reporting company)
EF/parameters required (factor keys): • None (reporting company collects emissions data from waste treatment companies; the waste company already used emission factors to calculate emissions)
Calculation steps:
1) Identify waste treatment providers handling waste from the reporting company.
2) Obtain the provider’s allocated Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions attributable to the reporting company’s waste.
3) Sum allocated emissions across waste treatment providers.

Method: Cat 5 — Waste generated in operations — Waste-type-specific
Equation (canonical): Σ (waste produced (tonnes or m3) × waste type and waste treatment specific emission factor (kg CO2e/tonne or m3))
Activity data required (fields):
• Waste produced (e.g., tonne, m3) and type of different waste generated in operations
• For each waste type, specific waste treatment method applied (e.g., landfilled, incinerated, recycled, etc.)
EF/parameters required (factor keys):
• Waste type-specific and waste treatment-specific emission factors (kg CO2e/tonne or kg CO2e/m3)
• Emission factors should include end-of-life processes only
• Emission factors may include emissions from transportation of waste (record flag)
Calculation steps:
1) For each waste type generated, record waste quantity (tonnes or m3).
2) Record the treatment method for each waste type.
3) Select EF specific to (waste type × treatment method) with end-of-life-only boundary.
4) Multiply waste quantity × EF.
5) Sum across waste types.

Equation (canonical):
Σ (distance_travelled_by_vehicle_type (vehicle-km or passenger-km) × EF_vehicle_type (kg CO2e/vehicle-km or kg CO2e/passenger-km))
+
(optional) Σ (hotel_nights × EF_hotel (kg CO2e/night))
Activity data required (fields):
• Total distance travelled by each mode of transport (air, train, bus, car, etc.) for all employees in reporting year
• Countries of travel (since EFs vary by country)
• Specific vehicle types used for travel (since EFs vary by vehicle type)
(optional) • Annual number of hotel nights
EF/parameters required (factor keys):
• Emission factors (kg CO2e per km or passenger-km) for each mode (aircraft, rail, metro, bus, taxi, etc.)
• For electric vehicles (if applicable), electricity emission factors per km or passenger-km
(optional) • Hotel emission factor (kg CO2e/night)
Calculation steps:
1) Aggregate distance travelled by mode/vehicle type (vehicle-km or passenger-km).
2) Select EF for each mode/vehicle type, matching country where possible.
3) Multiply distance × EF for each mode.
4) Optionally add hotels: hotel nights × EF_hotel.
5) Sum across vehicle types for Cat 6 total.

Equation (canonical):
Σ (fuel_consumed_liters × EF_fuel (kg CO2e/liter))
+
Σ (electricity_consumed_kWh × EF_electricity_grid (kg CO2e/kWh))
+
Σ (refrigerant_leakage_kg × GWP_refrigerant (kg CO2e/kg))
+
(optional) Σ (hotel_nights × EF_hotel (kg CO2e/night))

If fuel data unavailable:
Fuel_from_spend = fuel_spend / avg_fuel_price
Fuel_from_distance = Σ(distance_km × fuel_efficiency_l_per_km)
Activity data required (fields):
• Quantities of fuel consumed by fuel type (liters)
• Amount spent on fuel and average cost of fuel (if deriving liters)
• Fugitive emissions (e.g., refrigerant leakage) (kg)
If applicable:
• Distance travelled (km)
• Average fuel efficiency of vehicle (liters/km)
(optional)
• Annual number of hotel nights (nights)
EF/parameters required (factor keys):
• Life cycle fuel emission factors (kg CO2e/liter or per energy unit)
• Electricity emission factors for grid (kg CO2e/kWh)
• Fugitive emission factors / GWPs (kg CO2e/kg refrigerant leakage)
(optional)
• Hotel emission factor (kg CO2e/night)
(if deriving liters)
• Average fuel price ($/liter)
Calculation steps:
1) Collect fuel litres by type; if unavailable, derive litres from spend/price or from distance×fuel efficiency.
2) Multiply fuel litres × EF_fuel and sum across fuel types.
3) Add electricity emissions where applicable: kWh × EF_grid.
4) Add fugitive emissions where applicable: refrigerant leakage × GWP.
5) Optionally add hotels: hotel nights × EF_hotel.
6) Sum all components for Cat 6 total.

Equation (canonical): Σ (total_employees × %employees_using_mode × one_way_distance × 2 × working_days_per_year × EF_mode (kg CO2e per vehicle-km or passenger-km))
Activity data required (fields):
• Number of employees
• Average one-way commuting distance per day
• Average breakdown of transport modes used by employees (% mode split)
• Average number of working days per year
EF/parameters required (factor keys): • Emission factors for each mode of transport (usually per passenger-km; CO2/CH4/N2O or CO2e)
Calculation steps:
1) Capture total employees, average one-way distance, working days/year, and mode split.
2) For each mode, compute employees×%mode×distance×2×days.
3) Multiply by EF_mode.
4) Sum across modes.

Method: Cat 7 — Employee commuting — Distance-based (+ optional teleworking)
Equation (canonical):
Step 1: total_distance_by_vehicle_type = Σ(daily_one_way_home_to_work_km × 2 × commuting_days_per_year)
Step 2: commuting_emissions = Σ(total_distance_by_vehicle_type × EF_vehicle_type)
+
(optional teleworking) Σ(energy_consumed_kWh × EF_energy (kg CO2e/kWh))
Activity data required (fields):
• Total distance travelled by employees over the reporting period
• Mode of transport used for commuting (train, subway, bus, car, bicycle, etc.)
• Daily one-way distance home↔work and commuting days per year (or equivalent aggregated distance)
(optional teleworking)
• Quantities of energy consumed during teleworking (kWh) by energy source
EF/parameters required (factor keys):
• Emission factors for each commuting mode (usually per passenger-km; CO2/CH4/N2O or CO2e)
(optional teleworking)
• Emission factors for teleworking energy sources (kg CO2e/kWh)
Calculation steps:
1) Compute total distance by mode/vehicle type using daily one-way distance × 2 × commuting days.
2) Select EF per mode (passenger-km or vehicle-km as applicable).
3) Multiply total distance × EF per mode.
4) Optionally add teleworking energy emissions by energy source.
5) Sum across modes.

Equation (canonical):
Σ (fuel_consumed_liters × EF_fuel (kg CO2e/liter))
+
Σ (electricity_consumed_kWh × EF_electricity_grid (kg CO2e/kWh))
+
Σ (refrigerant_leakage_kg × GWP_refrigerant (kg CO2e/kg))

If fuel data unavailable:
Fuel_from_spend = fuel_spend / avg_fuel_price
Fuel_from_distance = Σ(distance_km × fuel_efficiency_l_per_km)
Activity data required (fields):
• Quantities of fuel consumed (liters) and fuel type
• Amount spent on fuel and average cost of fuel (if deriving liters)
• (If applicable) distance travelled and average fuel efficiency
EF/parameters required (factor keys):
• Life cycle fuel emission factors (kg CO2e/liter or energy basis)
• For electric vehicles (if applicable), electricity emission factors (kg CO2e/kWh)
Calculation steps:
1) Collect fuel litres (or derive from spend/price or distance×efficiency).
2) Multiply litres × EF_fuel.
3) Add electricity component if applicable.
4) Sum across commuting-related fuels/energy.

Equation (canonical):
For each leased asset:
Scope1_asset = Σ(fuel_liters × EF_fuel) + Σ(refrigerant_leakage_kg × EF_refrigerant) + process_emissions
Scope2_asset = Σ(electricity/steam/heating/cooling_kWh × EF_energy)
Then total = Σ (Scope1_asset + Scope2_asset)

If leased building not sub-metered:
Energy_use_leased_space = (reporting_company_area_m2 / building_total_area_m2) × building_occupancy_rate × building_total_energy_use_kWh
Activity data required (fields):
• Asset-specific fuel use; electricity/steam/heating/cooling use; process emissions; fugitive emissions (refrigerant leakage)
OR asset-specific Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions data
• (For non-submetered building allocation) reporting company area, building total area, building occupancy rate, building total energy use
EF/parameters required (factor keys):
• Site/region-specific emission factors for electricity and fuels per unit consumption (kg CO2e/kWh, kg CO2e/liter)
• Emission factors for fugitive and process emissions (kg CO2e/kg refrigerant leakage, etc.)
Calculation steps:
1) For each leased asset, compute Scope 1 from fuel + refrigerant leakage + process.
2) Compute Scope 2 from purchased electricity/steam/heating/cooling.
3) Sum Scope 1+2 for each asset, then sum across assets.
4) If leased building space not sub-metered, allocate energy use using area share × occupancy × building total energy and then compute emissions.

Equation (canonical):
Buildings: Σ (floor_space_by_building_type_m2 × EF_building_type (kg CO2e/m2/year))
Other assets / no floor space: Σ (asset_count_by_type × EF_asset_type (kg CO2e/asset/year))
Activity data required (fields):
• Floor space of each leased asset (m2)
• Number of leased assets, by building type; and/or
• Number of leased assets that give rise to Scope 2 emissions (e.g., company cars, trucks, etc.)
EF/parameters required (factor keys):
• Average emission factors by floor space (kg CO2e/m2/year)
• Average emission factors by building type (kg CO2e/building/year) (if used)
• Emission factors by asset type (kg CO2e/asset/year)
Calculation steps:
1) For buildings where floor space is available: multiply floor space × EF_building_type and sum across building types.
2) For non-building assets (or buildings with no floor space data): multiply asset count × EF_asset_type and sum across asset types.
3) Sum building and non-building totals for Cat 8.

Equation (canonical):
For each lessor:
Scope1_lessor = Σ(fuel_liters × EF_fuel) + Σ(refrigerant_leakage_kg × EF_refrigerant) + process_emissions
Scope2_lessor = Σ(electricity/steam/heating/cooling_kWh × EF_energy)
Allocated lessor emissions = (leased_asset_metric / total_lessor_asset_metric) × (Scope1_lessor + Scope2_lessor)
Total = Σ allocated lessor emissions
Activity data required (fields):
• Lessor’s fuel use, electricity use, process emissions and fugitive emissions (refrigerant leakage), OR lessor’s Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions data
• Physical or financial data for allocation (e.g., total area/volume/quantity of lessor’s assets and total area/volume/quantity of leased assets)
EF/parameters required (factor keys):
• Site/region-specific EFs for electricity and fuels (kg CO2e/kWh, kg CO2e/liter)
• EFs for fugitive and process emissions (kg CO2e/kg refrigerant leakage etc.)
Calculation steps:
1) For each lessor, compute Scope 1 emissions from fuel + refrigerant leakage + process.
2) Compute Scope 2 emissions from electricity/steam/heating/cooling.
3) Compute total lessor emissions = Scope1+Scope2.
4) Allocate lessor emissions to leased assets using physical/financial allocation factor (leased metric / total lessor assets).
5) Sum allocated emissions across lessors.

Equation (canonical): Σ (volume_stored (m3/pallet/TEU) × avg_days_stored × EF_storage (kg CO2e per m3-day or pallet-day or TEU-day))
Activity data required (fields):
• Volume of goods stored (m2/m3/pallet/TEU) or pallets
• Average number of days stored
• Throughput-based data (if needed)
EF/parameters required (factor keys): • Storage EF per pallet-day OR per m2/m3-day OR per TEU-day
Calculation steps:
1) Estimate volume-days.
2) Multiply volume × days × EF.
3) Sum across facilities.

Equation (canonical):
Facility emissions = (fuel_kWh × EF_fuel) + (electricity_kWh × EF_electricity) + (refrigerant_leakage_kg × EF_refrigerant_or_GWP)
Allocated facility emissions = (volume_company_goods_m3 / total_volume_goods_m3) × facility_emissions
Total = Σ allocated facility emissions
Activity data required (fields):
• Site-specific fuel, electricity use
• Site-specific refrigerant leakage
• Average occupancy rate / average volume stored
• Volume of reporting company goods in facility; total volume in facility
EF/parameters required (factor keys):
• Site/region-specific EFs for fuels and electricity (kg CO2e/kWh; kg CO2e/liter where applicable)
• Refrigerant emission factors / GWP (kg CO2e/kg leaked)
Calculation steps:
1) Compute facility emissions from fuel + electricity + refrigerants.
2) Allocate by volume share.
3) Sum across facilities.

Equation (canonical): Σ (mass_or_volume_goods (tonnes or TEU) × distance_leg_km × EF_mode_or_vehicle (kg CO2e per tonne-km or TEU-km))
Activity data required (fields):
• Mass or volume of products sold (tonnes or TEU)
• Distances travelled per leg (supplier data, maps, port-to-port)
• Mode/vehicle type per leg
EF/parameters required (factor keys): • Emission factor by mode/vehicle type per tonne-km or TEU-km (CO2/CH4/N2O or CO2e)
Calculation steps:
1) Collect legs: mass/volume, distance, mode.
2) Multiply mass/volume × distance × EF.
3) Sum across legs.

Equation (canonical):
Emissions = Σ(fuel_litres × EF_fuel)
+ Σ(electricity_kWh × EF_grid)
+ Σ(refrigerant_leakage_kg × GWP_refrigerant)

If fuel data unavailable:
Fuel_from_spend = fuel_spend / avg_fuel_price
Fuel_from_distance = Σ(distance_km × fuel_efficiency_l_per_km)

Allocated fuel use = total_fuel_consumed × (mass/volume_company_goods / mass/volume_goods_transported)
(Optional) backhaul emissions = Σ(fuel_backhaul × EF_fuel)
Activity data required (fields):
• Quantities of fuel consumed (litres) and fuel type; OR fuel spend + avg fuel price; OR distance travelled + fuel efficiency
• Amount of refrigerant leakage (kg)
If applicable: distance travelled, average fuel efficiency, mass of goods in vehicle (tonnes), refrigerated transport flag
EF/parameters required (factor keys):
• Fuel emission factors (kg CO2e/litre)
• Electricity grid factors (kg CO2e/kWh) (if EV)
• Refrigerant leakage factors / GWP (kg CO2e/kg)
• Average fuel price ($/litre) (if deriving)
Calculation steps:
1) Collect/derive fuel litres.
2) Compute total emissions from fuel + electricity + refrigerant leakage.
3) Allocate emissions to reporting company goods by mass/volume share.
4) Optionally include backhaul.
5) Sum across legs.

Equation (canonical): Σ (spend_on_transportation_by_type × EEIO_EF_transport (kg CO2e/$))
Activity data required (fields):
• Amount spent on transportation by type ($)
• Inflation data where applicable
EF/parameters required (factor keys): • EEIO / cradle-to-gate EF per $ for transportation type (kg CO2e/$)
Calculation steps:
1) Collect spend by transport type.
2) Normalize spend to EF base year if required.
3) Multiply spend × EF and sum.

Method: Cat 10 — Processing of sold products — Average-data
Equation (canonical): Σ (mass of sold intermediate product (kg) × EF_processing (kg CO2e/kg of final product))
Activity data required (fields):
• For each sold intermediate product type:
  - processes involved downstream to transform into usable final product
  - info needed for allocation (mass, economic value, etc.)
EF/parameters required (factor keys):
Either:
• Average emission factors for downstream processes (kg CO2e per kg of final product)
OR
• Life cycle emission factors of sold products and final products (to derive processing component)
Calculation steps:
1) Identify downstream processing route(s) per intermediate product.
2) Select EF_processing for the route.
3) Multiply mass sold × EF_processing.
4) Apply allocation if required.
5) Sum across intermediate products.

Method: Cat 10 — Processing of sold products — Site-specific
Equation (canonical):
Σ(fuel_consumed × EF_fuel_lifecycle)
+ Σ(electricity_consumed × EF_electricity_lifecycle)
+ Σ(refrigerant_leakage × GWP)
+ Σ(process emissions)
+ (where possible) Σ(waste_output_mass × EF_waste)
Activity data required (fields):
• Types and quantities of intermediate goods sold
Downstream data (either):
• Site-specific GHG emissions data from downstream partners, OR
• Site-specific activity data: quantities of electricity and fuels consumed; mass of waste generated; activity data for process/fugitive emissions
EF/parameters required (factor keys):
If site-specific activity data collected:
• Emission factors for fuels
• Emission factors for electricity
• (where possible) emission factors for waste outputs
• emission factors for process/fugitive emissions (if applicable)
If partner provides emissions directly: none needed (but record method).
Calculation steps:
1) Collect intermediate products sold.
2) Collect downstream partner emissions or activity data.
3) If activity data: multiply each activity by its EF (fuel, electricity, refrigerants, waste) and add process emissions.
4) Sum across downstream sites/processes.

Method: Cat 11 — Use of sold products — Direct use-phase (products that consume energy)
Equation (canonical):
Σ (lifetime_expected_uses × number_sold × fuel_per_use_kWh × EF_fuel (kg CO2e/kWh))
+
Σ (lifetime_expected_uses × number_sold × electricity_per_use_kWh × EF_electricity (kg CO2e/kWh))
+
Σ (lifetime_expected_uses × number_sold × refrigerant_leakage_per_use_kg × GWP_refrigerant (kg CO2e/kg))
Activity data required (fields):
• Total lifetime expected uses of product(s)
• Quantities of products sold
• Fuel used per use of product (kWh)
• Electricity consumption per use of product (kWh)
• Refrigerant leakage per use of product (kg)
EF/parameters required (factor keys):
• Emission factors for fuels (kg CO2e/kWh)
• Emission factors for electricity (kg CO2e/kWh)
• Emission factors / GWPs for refrigerants (kg CO2e/kg)
Calculation steps:
1) For each product group, define lifetime expected uses and units sold.
2) For each energy source, compute lifetime energy = lifetime_uses × units_sold × energy_per_use.
3) Multiply lifetime energy by the appropriate EF for fuel/electricity.
4) Compute refrigerant emissions = lifetime_uses × units_sold × leak_per_use × GWP.
5) Sum fuel + electricity + refrigerant components across products.

Method: Cat 11 — Use of sold products — Fuels and feed-stocks (combustion)
Equation (canonical): Σ (total_quantity_fuel_or_feedstock_sold (e.g., kWh) × combustion_EF_fuel_or_feedstock (kg CO2e/kWh))
Activity data required (fields): • Total quantities of fuels/feedstocks sold (by fuel type)
EF/parameters required (factor keys): • Combustion emission factors of fuel/feedstock (kg CO2e per unit, e.g., kg CO2e/kWh)
Calculation steps:
1) Collect quantities of fuels/feedstocks sold by type.
2) Select combustion EF per fuel/feedstock.
3) Multiply quantity × EF.
4) Sum across fuels/feedstocks.

Method: Cat 11 — Use of sold products — GHGs contained/emitted during use
Equation (canonical):
For each product or product group:
Use-phase emissions = (GHG_contained_per_product × number_sold × %released_over_lifetime × GWP_GHG)
Then total = Σ(use-phase emissions across products/groups)
Note: if %released unknown, assume 100%.
Activity data required (fields):
• Total quantities of products sold
• Quantity of GHG contained per product
• % of GHG released over product lifetime (if unknown, assume 100%)
EF/parameters required (factor keys): • GWP of the GHG contained in product (kg CO2e per kg GHG)
Calculation steps:
1) For each product/group, capture number sold and GHG mass contained per unit.
2) Determine fraction released over lifetime (or assume 1.0).
3) Multiply contained mass × units × fraction released × GWP.
4) Sum across products/groups.

Method: Cat 11 — Use of sold products — Indirect use-phase (scenario-weighted)
Equation (canonical):
Σ_scenarios( lifetime_uses × scenario_share × number_sold × fuel_per_use_in_scenario × EF_fuel )
+
Σ_scenarios( lifetime_uses × scenario_share × number_sold × electricity_per_use_in_scenario × EF_electricity )
+
Σ_scenarios( lifetime_uses × scenario_share × number_sold × refrigerant_leak_per_use_in_scenario × EF_refrigerant_or_GWP )
+
Σ_scenarios( lifetime_uses × scenario_share × number_sold × indirect_GHG_emitted_kg × GWP_GHG )
Activity data required (fields):
• Average number of uses over lifetime of product
• Use-phase scenarios and weights (% of lifetime uses)
• Fuel/electricity consumption per use in each scenario
• Refrigerant leakage per use in each scenario
• Indirect GHGs emitted in each scenario (kg)
EF/parameters required (factor keys):
• Combustion / electricity emission factors (kg CO2e per kWh)
• Refrigerant EF/GWP
• GWP of indirect GHGs
Calculation steps:
1) Define scenarios and weights summing to 1.0.
2) For each scenario, compute lifetime uses × scenario share × units sold.
3) Multiply by per-use energy and relevant EFs for fuels/electricity.
4) Add refrigerant + indirect GHG components.
5) Sum across scenarios.

Method: Cat 11 — Use of sold products — Intermediate products (direct energy consuming final products)
Equation (canonical): Σ (intermediate_products_sold × lifetime_uses_final_product × emissions_per_use_of_sold_intermediate_product (kg CO2e/use))
Activity data required (fields):
• Type(s) of final product(s) produced from reporting company’s intermediate product(s)
• % of intermediate product sales going to each final product type
• Activity data needed to calculate use-phase emissions of final product (same as direct/indirect use-phase methods)
EF/parameters required (factor keys): • Depending on final product type, emission factors required are the same as other Cat 11 use-phase methods (fuels, electricity, refrigerants, GWPs).
Calculation steps:
1) Identify final product types and allocation shares for intermediate products.
2) For each final product type, estimate lifetime uses and emissions per use attributable to the intermediate product.
3) Multiply intermediate products sold × lifetime uses × emissions per use.
4) Sum across final product types (weighted by shares).

Method: Cat 12 — End-of-life of sold products — Waste-treatment mix (waste-type-specific)
Equation (canonical): Σ (total_mass_sold_products_and_packaging_end_of_life_kg × %treated_by_method × EF_treatment_method (kg CO2e/kg))
Activity data required (fields):
• Total mass of sold products and packaging from point of sale to end-of-life after consumer use (kg), including packaging to point of retail and any packaging disposed prior to end-of-life of final product
• Proportion of this waste treated by different methods (% landfilled/incinerated/recycled/etc.)
EF/parameters required (factor keys): • Average waste treatment-specific emission factors based upon all waste disposal types (kg CO2e/kg)
Calculation steps:
1) Estimate total mass of sold products + packaging that becomes waste at end-of-life.
2) Determine disposal/treatment shares by method.
3) Select EF per treatment method (kg CO2e/kg).
4) Multiply mass × share × EF for each method.
5) Sum across treatment methods.

Equation (canonical):
For each leased asset:
Scope1_asset = Σ(fuel_liters × EF_fuel) + Σ(refrigerant_leakage_kg × EF_refrigerant) + process_emissions
Scope2_asset = Σ(electricity/steam/heating/cooling_kWh × EF_energy)
Total = Σ (Scope1_asset + Scope2_asset)

If leased building not sub-metered:
Energy_use_leased_space = (reporting_company_area_m2 / building_total_area_m2) × building_occupancy_rate × building_total_energy_use_kWh
Activity data required (fields):

• (Non-submetered buildings) reporting company area, building total area, occupancy rate, building total energy use
EF/parameters required (factor keys):

• EFs for fugitive/process emissions (incl. refrigerant GWPs)
Calculation steps:

3) Sum Scope 1+2 per asset and across assets.
4) If not sub-metered, allocate building energy from area share × occupancy × building total energy, then compute emissions.

Equation (canonical):
Buildings: Σ (floor_space_by_building_type_m2 × EF_building_type (kg CO2e/m2/year))
Other assets / no floor space: Σ (asset_count_by_type × EF_asset_type (kg CO2e/asset/year))
Activity data required (fields):
• Floor space of each leased asset
• Number of leased assets by building type; and/or
• Number of leased assets that give rise to Scope 2 emissions (e.g., company cars, trucks, etc.)
EF/parameters required (factor keys):
• Average emission factors by floor space (kg CO2e/m2/year)
• Average emission factors by building type (kg CO2e/building/year)
• Emission factors by asset type (kg CO2e/asset/year)
Calculation steps:
1) Apply floor-space EFs to leased buildings (if area data exists).
2) Apply per-asset EFs to non-building assets / where area missing.
3) Sum totals.

Equation (canonical):
For each lessee:
Scope1_lessee = Σ(fuel_liters × EF_fuel) + Σ(refrigerant_leakage_kg × EF_refrigerant) + process_emissions
Scope2_lessee = Σ(electricity/steam/heating/cooling_kWh × EF_energy)
Allocated lessee emissions = (leased_asset_metric / total_lessee_asset_metric) × (Scope1_lessee + Scope2_lessee)
Total = Σ allocated lessee emissions
Activity data required (fields):
• Lessee fuel use, electricity use, process emissions and fugitive emissions (refrigerant leakage), OR lessee Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions data
• Physical/financial allocation data: leased asset metric (area/volume/quantity) and total lessee asset metric
EF/parameters required (factor keys):
• Site/region-specific EFs for energy sources (kg CO2e/kWh; kg CO2e/liter)
• EFs for fugitive/process emissions
Calculation steps:
1) Compute Scope 1+2 for each lessee (or accept lessee-reported S1+S2).
2) Allocate lessee emissions to leased assets using leased metric / total lessee assets.
3) Sum allocated emissions across lessees.

Equation (canonical):
Leased buildings (floor space available): Σ (floor_space_by_building_type_m2 × EF_building_type (kg CO2e/m2/year))
Other assets / no floor space: Σ (asset_or_building_count × avg_emissions_per_asset_type (kg CO2e/asset/year))
Activity data required (fields):
• Floor space of each franchise (by building type) OR number of franchises by building type
• Number of franchise assets that give rise to Scope 2 emissions (e.g., company cars, trucks)
EF/parameters required (factor keys):
• Average emission factors by floor space (kg CO2e/m2/year)
• Average emission factors by building type (kg CO2e/building/year)
• Emission factors by asset type (kg CO2e/asset/year)
Calculation steps:
1) Apply floor-space EFs where area data exists.
2) Apply per-building/per-asset average EFs where only counts exist.
3) Sum across franchises/assets.

Equation (canonical):
Σ (scope 1 emissions + scope 2 emissions of each franchise)

If buildings not sub-metered:
Energy_use_franchise_kWh = (franchise_area_m2 / building_total_area_m2) × building_occupancy_rate × building_total_energy_use_kWh
Activity data required (fields):
Either:
• Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions data from franchisees, OR
• Site-specific fuel use, electricity use, and other process/fugitive emissions activity data
If not sub-metered:
• franchise area; building total area; building occupancy rate; building total energy use
EF/parameters required (factor keys):
If collecting fuel/energy data:
• Site/region-specific EFs for electricity and fuels (kg CO2e/kWh; kg CO2e/liter)
• EFs for process emissions (e.g., refrigeration/air conditioning; refrigerant GWPs)
If franchise provides emissions directly: none needed.
Calculation steps:
1) Collect franchise Scope 1+2 emissions (preferred).
2) If only energy/activity data: compute fuel + electricity + fugitive/process emissions using EFs.
3) If not sub-metered, allocate building energy by area share × occupancy × total energy.
4) Sum across franchises.

Equation (canonical): Σ ( (investee_revenue_$ × EF_sector (kg CO2e/$ revenue)) × equity_share_fraction )
Activity data required (fields):
• Sector(s) investee operates in
• Investee revenue (by sector if multi-sector)
• Investor equity share (%)
EF/parameters required (factor keys): • EEIO emission factors for relevant sectors (kg CO2e/$ revenue)
Calculation steps:
1) Map investee revenue to EEIO sector(s).
2) Multiply revenue × sector EF.
3) Multiply by equity share.
4) Sum across investees (and sectors).

Method: Cat 15 — Investments — Average-data (project finance / debt with known use, annual)
Equation (canonical):
Construction phase: Σ ( (construction_cost_$ × EF_construction_sector (kg CO2e/$)) × share_total_costs )
Operational phase: Σ ( (project_revenue_$ × EF_operating_sector (kg CO2e/$)) × share_total_costs )
Activity data required (fields):
• Project construction cost in reporting year (if construction phase) OR project revenue in reporting year (if operational phase)
• Investor proportional share of total project costs (equity + debt)
EF/parameters required (factor keys):
• EEIO emission factors for relevant construction sector (kg CO2e/$)
• EEIO emission factors for relevant operating sector (kg CO2e/$)
Calculation steps:
1) Determine phase (construction vs operational).
2) Multiply cost or revenue by sector EF.
3) Multiply by investor share of total project costs.
4) Sum across projects.

Equation (canonical): Σ (scope 1 and scope 2 emissions of equity investment × equity_share_fraction)
Activity data required (fields):
• Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions of investee company
• Investor’s proportional share of equity in the investee
• If significant: investee Scope 3 emissions (or estimate via average-data method)
EF/parameters required (factor keys): • None (reporting company collects emissions data from investees)
Calculation steps:
1) Collect investee Scope 1+2 emissions for reporting year.
2) Determine equity share (%).
3) Multiply emissions × equity share.
4) Sum across equity investments.

Method: Cat 15 — Investments — Project-specific (project finance / debt with known use, annual)
Equation (canonical): Σ (project_scope1+2_emissions_in_year × share_of_total_project_costs_fraction)
Activity data required (fields):
• Scope 1 and 2 emissions that occur in reporting year for relevant projects
• Investor proportional share of total project costs (equity + debt)
EF/parameters required (factor keys): • None (collect emissions data from investees/projects)
Calculation steps:
1) Collect project Scope 1+2 emissions for reporting year.
2) Determine investor share of total project costs.
3) Multiply emissions × share.
4) Sum across projects.

Equation (canonical): Σ ( (projected_annual_emissions × projected_lifetime_years) × share_of_total_project_costs_fraction )
Activity data required (fields):
• Expected average annual emissions of project
• Expected lifetime of project
• Investor share of total project costs (%)
• Assumptions on operation (e.g., capacity factor, heat rate, fuel carbon content) as applicable
EF/parameters required (factor keys): • None if projected annual emissions are provided/derived separately; otherwise depends on project type (e.g., fuel carbon content, heat rate)
Calculation steps:
1) Estimate projected annual emissions (project-specific engineering assumptions as needed).
2) Multiply by projected lifetime (years).
3) Multiply by investor share of total project costs.
4) Sum across projects.
